tutorial.button: How to spot a moving object
tutorial.title: How to spot a moving object
tutorial.p1: In a blink animation, every frame is a different epoch of the same patch of sky, scaled identically. A star that doesn't move will sit on the same pixel in every frame.
tutorial.p2: A moving object (like a nearby star with high proper motion) will visibly jump between frames — the same trick Clyde Tombaugh used to discover Pluto in 1930, and that NASA's Backyard Worlds citizen-science project still uses today with WISE images.
tutorial.p3: A variable object (like RW Aurigae or R Draconis) stays in the same place but changes brightness between frames.
tutorial.p4: Watch out for artifacts: single bright or dark pixels that appear in only one frame are usually cosmic-ray hits or bad pixels, not real sources. The flagged-pixel fraction in the metadata table tells you how much of each frame was masked out.
